argument_summary: The admissible record does not support a clean, caveat-free certification theory. It does support a narrower position: certification can be defended only on an aggregate-readiness basis if the auditor treats the current refund-workflow weakness as requiring explicit prelaunch disclosure or equivalent caveated treatment rather than as fully cured. The strongest admissible reading is that aggregate readiness passed by 2.2 points with no severity-one rehearsal incidents, while public governance guidance supports monitored deployment and documented limitations, but the unresolved refund-workflow gap, draft-status mitigation runbook, and model-card inconsistency prevent a clean policy showing.
claims_about_business_cost: Escalation cost exists, but business impact is not the basis for policy compliance. At most, the cost consideration supports avoiding unnecessary escalation if the auditor can resolve the issue through caveated treatment, corrected disclosure, and continued monitoring rather than treating the entire certification request as unsupported in all respects.
claims_about_policy: Enterprise policy is the controlling standard. Under the stated policy text, draft monitoring and general governance guidance do not substitute for either resolution of the weakness or an approved mitigation with the required fields. The actor therefore narrows its claim: the packet should not be read as proving clean certification without conditions. The admissible evidence is more consistent with caveated certification support if the refund-workflow limitation is disclosed for the named launch use case, because the current record shows a live disclosure issue rather than proof that no material limitation exists.
concessions: The enterprise refund workflow slice remains below target, concentrated in refund-policy summarization.
The mitigation artifact is still draft-quality because the rollback threshold and review date are TBD.
The model-card draft currently says there are no known material limitations even though admissible evidence shows a reviewer question about disclosing the refund-workflow issue.
General public guidance on monitoring and model cards is supportive context, not a substitute for the internal policy predicates.
